title: Get a home fire extinguisher ready to use: break the tamper seal and pull the pin
instruction: Get the fire extinguisher ready to use: break the tamper seal and pull out the safety pin without squeezing the lever, keeping the extinguisher standing where it is; drop the pin on the bench, then let go.
context: Pulling the safety pin is the first step of PASS (pull, aim, squeeze, sweep), the sequence the U.S. Fire Administration teaches households for using a fire extinguisher. On this home extinguisher, a tamper seal holds the ring pin in place. The task is to break the seal and withdraw the pin while keeping the lever released and the cylinder upright.
setup: On a flat wooden bench: a First Alert HOME1 class rechargeable home extinguisher (painted steel cylinder 3.25 in, 14.3 in overall, 5.4 lb; chrome valve with gauge and nozzle; black pressed-steel lever above a fixed carry handle) stands upright 0.42 m in front of the robot, centred between the arms, handle pointing away. A steel ring pin (3.2 x 50 mm, estimated) passes through the valve and lever; its steel wire ring (24 mm, estimated) hangs down toward the right arm. A plastic pull-tight tamper seal (9 in) ties the pin to the carry handle. Both arms start parked. Nothing else on the bench.
scoring: 1.0: the tamper seal is broken; the pin is fully out of the valve and resting on the bench; the lever never moved more than 1 deg (1.85 mm at the lever tip); at no time did the extinguisher slide more than 10 mm or lean more than 5 deg; both hands end at least 80 mm from the cylinder, valve, pin and ring; extinguisher and pin each move under 2 mm for 1 s. 0.5: the same, but the pin is withdrawn more than 5 mm and not yet out. 0 otherwise. Lever past 1 deg, a tip past 20 deg or the pin off the bench keeps the score at 0. Real trial: side video against a marked base outline and a mm scale behind the lever tip.
reset_notes: Push the pin back through the valve and lever from the ring side and fit a new UL-listed plastic tamper seal from the ring round the carry handle; one seal per trial. Real trials use a unit emptied and depressurised by a service shop.
fidelity: Rigid parts at HOME1 size and listed 2.45 kg; at an emptied unit's estimated 1.32 kg the demo still scores 1.0 (slide 0.1 mm, lean 0.3 deg). The seal is a breakable joint at UL 299's 65 N maximum (1.66 N m in twist, assumed 25.6 mm arm): slack pushed in, locked outward and in twist. The lever's tangs clear the pin by 0.6 mm; a squeeze binds it. Not modelled: discharge, pressure, gauge. Estimated: valve and lever shapes, pin 3.2 x 50 mm, ring 24 mm.
